clue.text: Trunk service interrupted by somebody drunk

indicators.note: a service that is interrupted has something breaking into the middle of it

parts.note: STD, subscriber trunk dialling, was the British long-distance phone service
somebody is anyone, one

explanation.surface: A long-distance phone call is cut short by a caller who has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: STD stands for subscriber trunk dialling, the old British system for long-distance calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: someone heavily intoxicated by drink or drugs is said to be this.

clue.text: He delivered thunderbolt services — breastplates needed!

parts.note: Thor, the Norse god of thunder, hurled thunderbolts
in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: A thunder god delivering blows needs armour plating to protect himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorax was the chest armour of ancient soldiers, so the plural names several pieces of chest armour.

clue.text: Duck has joint under the beak

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece under another is written after it

parts.note: beak is slang for the nose
a joint is a cheap bar or club, also called a dive

explanation.surface: A bird has a joint just below its bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird, but here it is the verb: to plunge down.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to drop sharply, as an aircraft does in a steep plunging descent.

clue.text: He had a fifth form with a name for order

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective naming a religious order, here standing for that order

parts.note: The Fifth Form at St Dominic's is a Victorian school story by Talbot Baines Reed, so the saint 'had' that form

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster in charge of the fifth form earns a reputation for keeping discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like discipline but is the religious order founded by St Dominic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Friars are the religious order founded by St Dominic in the 13th century.

clue.text: London street game

explanation.surface: A road in London named after a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous London street of gentlemen's clubs, and the old mallet-and-ball game played there that gave it its name.

clue.text: A sort of double entendre, typically Oxbridge?

definitions.text: A sort of double entendre, typically Oxbridge?

parts.words: A sort of double entendre, typically Oxbridge
parts.note: Oxbridge blends Oxford and Cambridge into one word carrying two meanings, a blend coined by Lewis Carroll's Humpty Dumpty

explanation.surface: A risque pun of the kind beloved of university wits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double entendre' suggests innuendo, but the clue means a single word packing two meanings, as Oxbridge packs two universities.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend word fuses parts of two words and their senses, as smog does smoke and fog.

clue.text: Opponent of change has old king tied in knots

parts.note: Lud was a legendary early king of Britain, remembered in Ludgate

indicators.note: something tied in knots is twisted out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A reactionary resists progress, keeping an ancient monarch tightly bound.
explanation.walkthrough: King Lud gives his name to Ludgate in London; 'in knots' scrambles the four letters that follow him.
explanation.definitionFit: The original machine-breakers resisted new technology, and the name now describes anyone hostile to innovation.

clue.text: Whirligig, or agouti perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters could form something else if rearranged

explanation.surface: A spinning toy is compared to a small South American rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging the letters of OR AGOUTI; an agouti is a rodent, an irrelevance.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose description: an early rotor aircraft whose unpowered blades spin freely like a toy windmill.

clue.text: One Formby leaned on for illumination

definitions.text: One Formby leaned on for illumination

parts.words: One Formby leaned on for illumination
parts.note: George Formby's comic song has him leaning on a street-light post at the corner of the street

explanation.surface: The comedian George Formby rests against something that gives light.
explanation.walkthrough: George Formby was a British ukulele-playing comedian famous for the song Leaning on a Lamp-post.
explanation.definitionFit: Street furniture holding a light aloft, the object in Formby's best-known song.

clue.text: Literary critic right about returning scholar's material

indicators.note: about means going round, so the critic and R surround the next piece

parts.note: Sir Edmund Gosse was a Victorian literary critic

indicators.note: returning means the scholar's letters are read backwards

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A critic straightens out a returning academic's manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like part of the scholar's possessions, but it is the definition; 'returning' and 'about' work in turn on the scholar's degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauzy, very fine fabric is named for the delicate cobweb threads it resembles.

clue.text: Morning duty to turn out the holy of holies

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters being turned around into a new order

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means morning

explanation.surface: An early-morning chore of clearing out the inner sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn out' rearranges AM plus DUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the innermost sanctuary of an ancient temple, entered only by priests.

clue.text: Praise by a lot of pit workers for old medicine

parts.note: to laud is to praise
the NUM, National Union of Mineworkers, is a body of British coal miners

explanation.surface: Miners are applauded for an old-fashioned remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM is the British coal miners' union.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture of opium widely prescribed as a painkiller and sedative in Victorian times.

clue.text: Call to keeper in the saddle

parts.note: a keeper is a ring worn to hold another ring in place on the finger
a rider who is up is mounted on the horse

explanation.surface: Shout to a gamekeeper sitting on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeper' suggests a goalkeeper or gamekeeper, but it is a guard ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to telephone someone.

clue.text: Surrounding district conquered by Caesar, for example — an about turn

parts.note: Caesar's boast veni, vidi, vici ends with vici, I conquered

indicators.note: an about turn faces the other way, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A region overrun by Julius Caesar who then turned round and left.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar's famous boast, 'I came, I saw, I conquered', supplies the first piece; 'about turn' then spins the last two short words as a block.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic word for neighbourhood or the area round about a place.

clue.text: Company board is for bridging operation

definitions.note: a description of use rather than a noun: what serves to bridge ship and shore

parts.note: a gang is a company of workers
a plank is a board

explanation.surface: A firm's directors are meeting to discuss a construction project over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company board' reads as directors, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A movable walkway laid between a ship and the quay to cross the gap.

clue.text: Man perhaps misled struck-off doctor

indicators.note: a struck-off doctor is removed from the register, so the doctor's letters are taken out

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A man may have been deceived by a disgraced physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Man is one such island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Viennese heroine is a Miss Wilfer

parts.note: Bella Wilfer is a heroine of Dickens's Our Mutual Friend

explanation.surface: A Viennese leading lady turns out to be a Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: The Viennese heroine is from Shakespeare's Measure for Measure, set in Vienna.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's novice nun in Measure for Measure, whose chastity drives the plot set in Vienna.

clue.text: Apply pointed remark to turner doing shift work

parts.note: to lay is to apply, as paint on a wall
a shaft is a barbed or pointed comment

explanation.surface: Make a cutting remark to a lathe operator working shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turner' looks like a lathe worker; it is a rotating part, and 'shift' is gear shifting.
explanation.definitionFit: In a gearbox, the secondary rotating rod that carries the gears used when changing gear.

clue.text: Garment removed by stripper

parts.note: reads as a striptease, but a paint stripper removes a layer of paint of the same name as the garment

explanation.surface: An item of clothing taken off by a striptease artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripper is paint stripper, and what it removes is a layer of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: An outer garment, and also a layer of paint, which is what paint stripper strips.

clue.text: Boy showing diligence

explanation.surface: A lad displaying hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diligence' looks like hard work, but a diligence was a stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, and a closed four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, as a diligence was a public coach.

clue.text: Ill-fated crusade about vivisection

indicators.note: vivisection cuts up a living body, so the letters are cut up and reassembled

parts.note: C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A doomed campaign against experiments on live animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vivisection' rearranges CRUSADE with C.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: under a curse, doomed to misfortune.

clue.text: Kind of student who has learnt in revolution

indicators.note: something in revolution is turned over, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A student who has studied the history of uprisings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' rearranges LEARNT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a university student attending in person, as opposed to studying by correspondence.

clue.text: Silly impulse over cow girl with, a twitch

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece over another is written before it

parts.note: in Freudian theory the id is the source of instinctive impulses
Io was a maiden turned into a heifer by Zeus
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A foolish whim leaves a cowgirl twitching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow girl' suggests a cowgirl; it is Io of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: foolish, as an idiot would be.

clue.text: It heightened the tragedy of ancient Greece

definitions.text: It heightened the tragedy of ancient Greece

parts.words: It heightened the tragedy of ancient Greece
parts.note: Greek tragic actors wore thick-soled boots that raised them up on stage

explanation.surface: Something intensified the drama of Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heightened' suggests intensifying, but it means literally making the actors taller.
explanation.definitionFit: The thick-soled half-boot of Greek tragic actors, which came to symbolise tragedy itself.

clue.text: Blow to higher return for the unions

parts.note: upper means higher

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the unions' letters run backwards

parts.note: the TUC, Trades Union Congress, is the British federation of unions

explanation.surface: A setback for the trade unions demanding more pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress; 'return' turns it to CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing punch thrown upward under the opponent's chin.

clue.text: Shed pawn lost in battle

indicators.note: a lost piece is gone from the board, so its letter leaves the word

parts.note: Lepanto was a 1571 sea battle against the Ottoman fleet
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess pawn gets taken during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a verb but is a noun, a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut with a single sloping roof built against a wall.

clue.text: Egg-shaped head is H. Dumpty's attribute

parts.note: oval means egg-shaped
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Humpty Dumpty has an egg-shaped head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like Humpty's head, but is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Humpty Dumpty is an egg, so his defining quality is being rounded and elongated.

clue.text: Bound as an apprentice to object ..to dead-end

parts.note: an article is an object or item

indicators.note: end picks out the final letter of the word dead

explanation.surface: A trainee is indentured to a job with no prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead-end' reads as a hopeless job; it is the final letter of 'dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainee solicitors and accountants were formerly bound by contract, or articles, to a firm.

clue.text: Works to make dough for necessities, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, giving one of identical sound

parts.note: needs are necessities

explanation.surface: A baker labours for the basic necessities of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' suggests money, but it is bread dough.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker presses and folds bread mixture by hand.
